newsitem.title: ITALY: BT not interested in Stet stake-rept.
newsitem.headline: BT not interested in Stet stake-rept.

text.p: British Telecom is not interested in forming an alliance with Italian state telecom group Stet, said BT's chief executive officer Peter Bonfield in interviews with Italian newspapers.
"We prefer having Stet as a rival than as an ally. We want to compete with European public monopolies," Bonfield told Rome daily La Repubblica.

Bonfield said that he was optimistic that the planned privatisation of Stet would be a success. "I am sure that the operation (privatisation) will be a success but we have other programmes to follow."
Talks were under way with energy group ENI to take over the telecommunications infrastructure operated by Eni subsidiary Snam.
"It is no secret that we are seeking an alliance with ENI on infrastructures. I think we will reach an agreement in the first quarter of 1997," Bonfield told the newspaper.
BT and its Italian allies in Albacom, a joint venture company in which BNL and Mediaset hold stakes, have already set up a company to bid for Italy's third mobile phone operating company.

BT and its allies would bid for the licence "if conditions of profitability can be correctly evaluated on which to calibrate investments and set up a service which is fully satisfactory to clients," Bonfield told Milan business paper Il Sole 24 Ore.
